Short answer
- Pick an integrated LED task lamp that is ENERGY STAR–rated (or at least specifies lumens, wattage and lm/W), dimmable, and offers adjustable color temperature and arm/angle control. From your catalog memory I found a product named Meadowlight Lamp that looks like a candidate, but I don’t have any verified specs for it — its energy claims will need to be confirmed before buying.

What I found in your catalog memory
- Entries: “Meadowlight Lamp”, “adjustable desk lamps”, “task lamps”, “lighting products”, “desk accessories”.
- Evidence status: the memory shows the Meadowlight Lamp name only; there are no provenance or spec extracts attached. In short: the catalog contains a candidate name, but no usable technical evidence (wattage, lumens, certification, etc.).

What to look for (selection checklist — verify each on the product page or spec sheet)
1. Energy efficiency
   - Rated lumens (lm) and input power (W). Calculate efficacy = lm ÷ W (look for ≥80 lm/W for a good office lamp; higher is better).
   - ENERGY STAR or equivalent certification (if available).
2. Light output and task suitability
   - Lumens: ~400–1000 lm for typical desk tasks (choose within that range depending on task intensity).
   - Recommended illuminance at the desk: ~300–500 lux for office tasks.
3. Color quality
   - Color temperature: 3500–4000 K (neutral white) commonly preferred for offices.
   - CRI (color rendering index): CRI ≥ 80 acceptable; CRI ≥ 90 is better if color accuracy matters.
4. Control features that save energy
   - Dimming capability (reduces power use when full output isn’t needed).
   - Occupancy or motion sensor and/or automatic shutoff.
   - Scheduling or smart controls to prevent unnecessary on-time.
5. Electrical/driver quality
   - Flicker rating or driver specs (look for “flicker-free” or low flicker % for comfort).
6. Lifecycle & maintenance
   - Rated lifetime (hours), warranty length, and whether LED modules are replaceable.
7. Physical ergonomics
   - Adjustable arm/head, glare control, stable base — to use light efficiently and avoid wasted light.

Example of an energy-savings check (how to verify claimed savings)
- If a lamp specification shows 10 W and produces the same usable light as an older 60 W incandescent:
  - Annual energy saved = (60 W − 10 W) × hours used/year.
  - Example: 50 W × 2,500 hours/year = 125,000 Wh = 125 kWh/year.
  - At $0.15/kWh that is ≈ $18.75 saved per lamp per year.
- Claim to verify: product’s actual wattage, lumen output (so you’re comparing equivalent light), and realistic hours of use.

Claims that need verification for Meadowlight Lamp (and any product)
- “Energy-efficient” or “saves X% energy” — verify wattage, lumens, and comparison baseline.
- “ENERGY STAR certified” — check official listing or spec sheet.
- Lumens per watt (lm/W) — confirm from spec sheet, not marketing copy.
- CRI, color temperature, and flicker performance — confirm numeric specs.
- Lifetime hours and warranty — verify in documentation.

Recommendation / next step
- If you want a single product recommendation from your catalog, I can:
  1) try to fetch full specs for Meadowlight Lamp and compare them to the checklist, or
  2) if you prefer, I can list 2–3 specific lamp models (ENERGY STAR LED task lamp; adjustable high-efficacy LED with motion sensor; smart desk lamp with scheduling) if you give a budget, style preference, and whether you want smart features or motion sensors.
Which would you like me to do? If you want me to check Meadowlight Lamp now, I’ll pull its spec sheet and verify the claims I listed.
